column1: # Hand-written expectations for the classifier route.
# Each row is <path>\t<offset>\t<mask>: the 32-byte window at <offset> in <path>
# (used as given, relative to the repository root) and the mask the classifier
# must return for it, as `0x` and eight lowercase hex digits.  Lines beginning
# with `#` and empty lines are not rows.
# The classifier marks twelve bytes: the six RFC 8259 structural characters
# `{ } [ ] : ,`, the quote `"` and the backslash `\` (the eight `IsStructuralB`
# bytes, the last two being the classifier's own string business), and RFC
# 8259's four whitespace bytes — space, tab, line feed and carriage return.
# Every byte of every pad window is `[`, space or `]`, all marked, so the mask
# is 0xffffffff; these rows are a no-regression set, not a discriminator.
# mixed.block interleaves those twelve classes with ordinary content.  Hand
# (`,`), 22 (`{`) and 28 (`}`) are structural; bits 10, 12, 24 and 27 are the
# quote; bit 25 is the backslash; bits 1, 2, 5, 9, 13, 15, 18, 23 and 30 are
# space, 8 line feed, 20 tab and 29 carriage return; bits 3 (`1`), 6 (`2`), 11
# content and are clear.  With all eight structural bytes counted, that is
# 0x7bd6f7b7 — not read back from maskOfList — and a body returning a constant
# all-ones mask cannot produce it.  The file is emitted by
# `leanllvm-json-classify --emit-block` and pinned by check.sh.
# The object arm establishes agreement with the compiled candidate on aligned
# windows only; see probes/json/classify_driver.c for the alignment gap.
